summary: Today’s pulse tracks Philippines wins first Eurovision Song Contest Asia, Sotheby's auction of $180m Van Gogh challenged over claims it was 'sold under duress', and Family of Watford woman set alight ‘desperate for answers’ after attack. Across BBC and Guardian, the strongest repeated signals are patients, cancer, and family. In the background, Copper wire upgrade caused nationwide flight suspension, US transport secretary says and US officials say flight stoppage stemmed from ‘routine maintenance’ as travel chaos continues keep the wider picture in motion.

headlines.title: Philippines wins first Eurovision Song Contest Asia
headlines.description: Front-runner Carmelle wins with 211 points for her women's empowerment anthem Sobra-Sobra.

headlines.title: Sotheby's auction of $180m Van Gogh challenged over claims it was 'sold under duress'
headlines.description: Sotheby's says it will work with the heirs of a family who had previously owned the artwork to try and reach a solution.

headlines.title: Family of Watford woman set alight ‘desperate for answers’ after attack
headlines.description: Appeal for information comes after Brenda Raymond, 80, was set on fire outside her flat on Monday The family of an elderly woman who was set on fire outside a block of flats in Watford have said that they are “desperate for answers”. Brenda Raymond, 80, was found set alight outside her flat on Caractacus Cottage View on Monday. She was taken to a nearby hospital, where she is in critical condition.

headlines.title: Copper wire upgrade caused nationwide flight suspension, US transport secretary says
headlines.description: The US government is trying to find out whether the chaos was caused by "incompetence" or faulty equipment.

headlines.title: US officials say flight stoppage stemmed from ‘routine maintenance’ as travel chaos continues
headlines.description: Thousands of flights still canceled as officials blamed ageing air control system for nationwide grounding The Trump administration says Friday’s four-hour nationwide Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) ground stop that delayed or canceled thousands of flight stemmed from routine maintenance. At a news briefing on Saturday, the US transportation secretary, Sean Duffy, said that the issues began when a contractor was performing “routine maintenance” at a remote FAA facility to “switch telecommunications lines” from copper wire to fiber optic cable.

headlines.title: NHS England on track to miss key cancer treatment target by 10,000 patients
headlines.description: Exclusive: 2,850 more patients a month would need to be treated within 62 days to meet March 2027 goal, as experts warn of failure of leadership Nearly 10,000 more cancer patients in England will not be treated on time because the government will fail to meet its targets, amid a failure of leadership, focus and resource, experts have warned. The NHS set an interim target to treat 80% of cancer patients within 62 days of urgent referral or consultant upgrade by March 2027. But with little more than 100 days to go, the proportion of patients starting treatment on time in September was 70.7%, down from 71.9% in August, NHS figures show.

headlinePool.title: Democrat wins Alaska governor’s seat for first time in nearly 30 years
headlinePool.description: Jonathan Kreiss-Tomkins’ victory means Democrats will now hold 30 US governorships after midterm blowout Democrats have captured Alaska ’s governor’s seat for the first time in nearly three decades, marking another major victory for their party in a midterm election period that has dramatically shifted political power across the US. Former Alaska state legislator Jonathan Kreiss-Tomkins defeated three Republican opponents, including a candidate backed by Donald Trump , becoming the first Democrat elected governor of Alaska since 1998.

headlinePool.title: FAA blames Friday's ground stop on 'equipment issue' during telecoms network upgrade
headlinePool.description: Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said initial investigations pointed to an issue with contractor L3Harris updating old tech at a remote location.

headlinePool.title: Cold weather health alerts issued for parts of UK on Sunday night
headlinePool.description: UKHSA warns of threat to vulnerable people from frosty conditions expected to last until Thursday More cold health alerts have been issued for parts of the UK on Sunday night and next week. The alerts were issued by the UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA) for the north-west, West Midlands and Yorkshire and the Humber, and will be in place from 9pm on Sunday until 9am on Thursday.

headlinePool.title: Italy fines Meta €805m over accessing users' photos
headlinePool.description: The social media giant is accused of not informing 20 million users it had access to their photos.

headlinePool.title: Fuel crisis and protests pressure Chile's far-right president
headlinePool.description: Chile's far-right President José Antonio Kast is facing mounting public anger, as rising fuel prices trigger transport strikes and protests across the country.

headlinePool.title: A rapid interest rate rise seems inevitable – and households are expected to pick up the tab
headlinePool.description: Raising borrowing costs too far risks laying waste to whatever growth there is in the economy A head of steam is building up behind the Bank of England raising interest rates again. With the latest forecasts by the central bank showing inflation rising to 5% next spring, another increase in the cost of borrowing seems inevitable, and may come as soon as next month. A growing number of analysts predict the Bank’s policymakers will don Scrooge masks when they meet on 17 December to deliver a message of austerity and sacrifice.

headlinePool.title: Trump, Putin and Xi plan historic joint meeting in China next week, White House says
headlinePool.description: Trump will discuss the "reduction of nuclear weapons" during the unprecedented talks, a spokeswoman says.

headlinePool.title: Nigeria cautions against travel via Ethiopia's main airport due to altitude
headlinePool.description: The foreign ministry in Abuja says 6 Nigerians with underlying health problems have died this year while transiting through Addis Ababa.

headlinePool.title: Andy Burnham says UK has ‘lost more than we gained’ through Brexit
headlinePool.description: PM accuses Tories of burning ‘all our bridges’ and says deal he is pursuing with EU will ‘get food prices down’ Andy Burnham has said the UK has “lost more than we gained” since leaving the EU, the prime minister’s latest in a string of comments criticising Brexit. Outlining his desire to form closer ties with Brussels, Burnham accused the Conservative party of having “burned all our bridges” with the bloc after Brexit and said a new deal he hopes to secure with the EU next week will “get food prices down” and put more money in the pockets of British exporters.
